units.translation: Appoint the best men, chosen from the city, to command at the gates with speed.
One man to be leader of all sheep-nurturing Asia.

Thus I emended what is in M ξύμφρονα τὰν γᾶν [concordant with the land], from which Triclinius made ξύμφονα ταγάν [concordant command] with a metrical fault: for ταγή [command] has a short first syllable.
The young leader of the blessed gods.
Commander of fifty times five ships.
Commanders of the ships that were left.
The two-throned power of the Achaeans, the concordant leaders of the youth of Hellas.
M ξύμφρονα τὰν γᾶν [concordant with the land]
But of the wretched mortals he had no account.
Who then, O wretched one, addresses me, the miserable one, with such true words?
What time will there be for the miserable woman?
Weighing down the scales with unequal fortune.
But your yoke of the balance is wholly.
Ares, the gold-exchanger of bodies and holder of the scales in the battle of the spear.

Thus Wordsworth, as Euripides Hipp. 1236 said ὦ πατρὸς τάλαιν᾽ ἀρά [O wretched curse of my father]: in M τελεῖ (εία, as it seems, a later hand wrote above), μέλαιν᾽ [black] Weilius, comparing line 832.
I am yoked to these necessities, wretched.
But now I, wretched, have suffered a heavenly tossing, a joy to my enemies.
Did the wretched one, on foot or as a sailor, make this attempt in folly?
I, wretched, have been struck by so great an army.
For the hostile (sic from the copy for αἰσχρά [shameful]) curse of my father, wretched, settles on my dry, tearless eyes.
Ah, wretched me, from evil misfortune.
Ah, wretched me, from the army that has been destroyed.
But I, dishonored, wretched, heavy in anger.
Around your shores, wretched, I wandered with offerings.
But now I, wretched, learn that he is dead.
Again some gadfly stings me, wretched.
Why have you brought me, wretched, here?
From a wretched mother and an unhappy father.
Wretched madness, first cause of sorrow.
O woman, wretched in many things, but wise in many.
O wretched child-destroying daughter of Thestius.
ὦ πατρὸς τάλαιν᾽ ἀρά [O wretched curse of my father]
In the plural Tανταλίδαι, descendants of Tantalus
O divine power, who falls upon the house and the two-natured sons of Tantalus.
Schol. καὶ οἱ ταχυδρόμοι οὐ δύνανταί με ἐκφυγεῖν [and the swift runners cannot escape me].
I bring down the edge of my foot; for the limbs of the swift runners are slippery.
καὶ οἱ ταχυδρόμοι οὐ δύνανταί με ἐκφυγεῖν [and the swift runners cannot escape me]
